# How Controlled Inputs Work

#### Course: Build your First Web App with React

## How Controlled Inputs Work

This is the code we previously wrote:

```react
<input
  type="text"
  placeholder="Entry title"
  value={title}
  onChange={(e) => setTitle(e.target.value)}
/>
```

Here, the two attributes do the following:

- value={title} tells the input what to display. Instead of the browser tracking the text internally, React feeds the value from state.
- onChange={(e) => setTitle(e.target.value)} runs on every keystroke. It reads the new text from e.target.value and saves it into the state.

Every time the user types, the state updates. Every time the state updates, React re-renders the input with the new value.

Thus, the input and the state are always in sync.
